title: RunLog
description: Append-only execution trace for one engine run (one pursuit, one pipeline execution). Distinct from feedback-event (human signal, feeds the flywheel): the run log is MACHINE signal — what the agents did, what they read, what they spent, what they decided. Written to <pursuit>/runs/<run_id>/run.jsonl as one JSON object per line; this schema describes a single line. A run is reconstructable by replaying the lines in order.

run_id.description: Stable ID for this execution. Replays get a fresh run_id and reference the original via replay_of.

seq.description: Monotonic sequence within the run. Ordering is by seq, not timestamp — parallel subagents share wall-clock.

record_type.description: One line per event. agent_call/tool_call are the token- and cost-bearing records; kb_retrieval is the provenance record that answers 'why did it say this?'.

stage.description: Which pipeline stage this record belongs to. Mirrors ARCHITECTURE_V2 pipeline names so the dashboard can group without a lookup table. gate_0 (P15/B70) is the intake-review gate; its in-chain decision logs into the intake stage run and this value carries only the resume-after-stop mini-run. assistant (P14/B63) is the steward-assistant lane, never a pipeline stage — its records live in the support workspace, structurally outside pursuit aggregation.

agent.description: Agent/subagent name, e.g. intake_analyst, kb_mapper, section_drafter, claim_auditor, buyer_red_team, revision_agent.

parent_span.description: seq or span id of the enclosing record — gives the trace its tree shape for parallel drafters.

model.description: Exact model id used (not the tier). Required on agent_call — model routing is a live variable and telemetry is worthless without it.

tool.description: tool_call records: tool name (card_search, open_document, web_fetch, write_back…).

tool_args_digest.description: Hash or short rendering of arguments. Full args only when sensitivity allows — never raw client text in a log that leaves the pursuit workspace.

tool_result_digest.description: tool_call records (P14/B63 — the first emitter): digest of the tool's returned payload, same raw-text-never-rides-a-line discipline as tool_args_digest. Absent when the tool refused before producing one.

kb.description: kb_retrieval records — the citation trail. Every drafted section must be traceable to the cards that fed it.

step.description: cite (B31): one section-scoped line carrying the drafter's surviving cards_cited — the WP9 edit_survival join input. Not a tool invocation; the opens preceding it are. path_descend (P13/C10, WP13 R9): the within-document navigation move — siblings/parent/children of a card via its canonical model, one file read, no catalog scan.

cards_opened.description: kb_ids actually opened — the subset that could have influenced output.

cards_cited.description: kb_ids the agent claims it used. Feeds edit_survival attribution when the reviewer later edits this text.

excluded.description: kb_ids withheld by policy — REPLAY HYGIENE: on a replay this holds the pursuit's own response. Auditable proof the engine did not read the answer key.

empty_result.description: true when card search returned nothing usable — the precondition for a legitimate gap rather than an invention.

facets.description: card_search (P13/C10, WP13 R9): the facet filter applied, facet name -> accepted values. ON the line so the retrieval replays from the log alone — the bare-query rule generalized: the LINE is sufficient.

path.description: path_descend: the anchor card's doc_path. Navigation context, never a retrieval key (KB10).

relation.description: path_descend: which neighborhood of the anchor was walked.

catalog_size.description: card_search (P13/C10): searchable cards at query time — the denominator catalog_scan_cost_share reads (B51's carrier). When lanes joined, this counts the UNION universe — the one idf was computed over.

lanes.description: card_search (P17/C1, B75§3a): the memory lanes whose catalogs joined this search. ABSENT on firm-only lines — every pre-P17 line replays byte-identically. REPLAY RESOLUTION (the line is sufficient): absent -> firm store; 'pursuit' -> <workspace>/<pursuit_id>/memory (pursuit_id is on every line); 'org' -> <workspace>/orgs/<kb.org_id>/memory.

org_id.description: card_search (P17/C1): the org whose memory lane joined, when lanes includes 'org' — on the line so replay never consults the brief. Opaque org_NNNN id; org NAMES live only in file content, never here (B75§2).

target.description: What this record was working on, so per-section telemetry rolls up without parsing prose.

slot_ref_id.description: Path A: the buyer's own numbering from the target-slot fixture.

gate.description: gate records — human decision points. On automated replay these are auto-approved; auto_approved MUST be true then, so replay results are never mistaken for human-approved output.

notes.description: The decider's notes, verbatim (P26a, P1-15): a rejection's rationale is the redo instruction and the audit record — it was mandatory at Gate 0 and Gate 2 and then discarded, or overwritten by the next decision. The run log is append-only, so it survives here.

wait_ms.description: Human latency — separated from compute latency so cycle-time reporting can tell the two apart.

validation.description: validation records — one per check per section. The audit trail behind the annotated draft.

check.description: anonymization and pre_export_leakage added by B13, injection_screen by B18 — each a metric that filtered on values the enum lacked (REPORTING_SPEC's 'injection screen flags'). extraction added by P12/C10 (B51's named carrier): per-document flag/pass for degraded extraction and the two-path diff. reconciliation added by P13/C10 (WP13 R6): per-re-ingest flag/pass — flag when anything drifted or orphaned, pass when all matched/created.

fact_sheet_ref.description: kb_id of the Fact Sheet entry that verified (or failed to verify) a Tier-1 claim.

gap.description: gap records — the engine asked instead of inventing. Gap rate and resolution time are day-one dashboard metrics; they are computed from these lines.

artifact.description: artifact records — every durable output written, with a content hash so a run can be verified reproducible.

run.description: run_start / run_end / cost_rollup records — the run's own header and footer.

mode.description: replay/regression_bench runs MUST be excluded from production telemetry aggregates. handoff runs (P20/B81) carry real judgment through the operator seam with no API and no marginal dollar; cost-bearing aggregates already admit only run.mode == 'live'.

config_digest.description: Hash of the effective config — research_mode, effort_allocation, model routing, gate collapse toggle. Two runs with the same digest are comparable; different digests explain divergence.

kb_snapshot.description: KB version/commit at run time. Without this, comparing two runs weeks apart compares two different knowledge bases and attributes the difference to the engine.

pursuit_kb_snapshot.description: run_start (P17/C1): snapshot of the pursuit's own memory lane (<pursuit>/memory) when non-empty — the kb_snapshot philosophy extended: two runs compare only when BOTH universes match (B75§3b).

org_kb_snapshot.description: run_start (P17/C1): snapshot of the linked org's memory lane when joined. Absent when no org is linked or its lane is empty.

notes.description: Free text. Not parsed by the dashboard — for human debugging only.

then.description: B10: 'model required on agent_call' was prose-only. Cost attribution and model-routing telemetry are worthless without the exact id.
